run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T10:27:50Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by a real, sustained failure of frontend-proxy's calls to its 'frontend' upstream: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR from about 10:03 onward (0 at 10:03:50, then 1.3-8.4 error spans per 10 minutes, still 2.08 at 10:42:50), and its access log shows HTTP 503 with flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} against the frontend cluster, first observed 10:03:07 and repeated through 10:37:44. The failing traces contain the frontend-proxy ingress span and its child 'router frontend egress' span (error=true, http.status_code=0) but no frontend span at all, while successful requests in the same traces do produce frontend 200 spans, so those connections were terminated before the frontend handled the request. The frontend service itself shows zero error spans and its pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and no lastState on pressure-free nodes, so it was not down. The stop mechanism is unobserved: the frontend container emitted no log lines, and the small CPU limits (frontend 100m, frontend-proxy 30m) leave the frontend 31-35% CFS-throttled, a measurement that starts after onset and has no pre-onset baseline. A separate real change, the chaos-mesh NetworkChaos experiments otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition-* applied from 10:25:49 to two fraud-detection pods and the kafka pod, is rejected as the cause because the first 503 (10:03:07) and others at 10:17:43 and 10:21:11/10:21:59 precede it and it targets a different path. Conclusion is partial: affected entity and failing path are established, the terminating mechanism is not.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans rose from 0 at 10:03:50 to 1.28 and 1.16 at 10:05:50 and 10:07:50, peaked around 8.4 per 10 minutes near 10:30:50 and were still 2.08 at 10:42:50; all of this service's error spans are on span_name 'ingress' (ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR non-zero, 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0).

frontend-proxy access logs show 503 with response flag UC and response code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} for upstream cluster 'frontend' at 10:03:07.225, 10:09:55, 10:10:51, 10:11:34, 10:17:43.749, 10:21:11 (GET / and GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO), 10:21:59.712, 10:26:27, 10:26:38, 10:27:11, 10:27:39, 10:29:07 and 10:37:44.492, affecting GET /, /api/products/{id} and /api/data.

In failing traces the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span has error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR and its child 'router frontend egress' span has error="true", http.status_code="0"; no frontend span exists in those traces, whereas successful POST /api/cart requests in the same traces produce frontend spans with http.status_code=200 and grpc.oteldemo.CartService status 0.

The frontend service reported zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on every operation series returned (GET, GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/*, grpc.oteldemo.*, dns.lookup, tcp.connect) while continuing to serve roughly 11k-16k spans per 5-10 minutes.

In the per-service error-span series, frontend, checkout, payment and accounting were 0, frontend-proxy was largest (about 1-6 per 10 minutes), and ad (about 1 per 10 minutes), fraud-detection (about 2 per 10 minutes) and recommendation (about 1 per 10 minutes) were low but non-zero.

Pods frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t (owner ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq are Running, Ready and ContainersReady since 09:48:55 and 09:48:58 with restartCount 0, empty lastState and no termination reason; deployments frontend and frontend-proxy each report 1 desired, 1 available, 1 ready, 1 updated, and no Pod events exist for either pod.

Deployment frontend container 'frontend' (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend) has limits cpu 100m and memory 200Mi, and deployment frontend-proxy container 'frontend-proxy' has limits cpu 30m and memory 50Mi.

The frontend container is CFS-throttled in 31-35% of periods (0.306-0.354) with a throttled-period rate of 4.3-6.8 per second between 10:04 and 10:40 while using only about 0.053 cores of its 0.1-core limit; frontend-proxy is throttled 0.056-0.077 while using about 0.014 of 0.03 cores; frontend working set rose slowly from about 122.8 MB to about 128.8 MB, below its 200Mi limit.

chaos-mesh NetworkChaos experiments named otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition-* (13 instances) were Started and Applied from 10:25:49 through 10:37:49, each logged TimeUp and Recovered about 55 seconds later, and their messages name only otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-29vm9; the related PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events reference those same three pods.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines every fault-injection flag with defaultVariant "off": adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure.

All five nodes are Ready with NetworkUnavailable, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False; frontend and frontend-proxy both run on node i-029c97e90b3730286; Services frontend, checkout and frontend-proxy each have exactly one ready endpoint (frontend to pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t at 100.96.4.88:8080).

A frontend outage is not supported: frontend has zero error spans on all span names with steady span volume, its pod is Ready with restartCount 0 and no OOMKilled or Evicted condition, and the nodes are pressure-free. A frontend-proxy pod restart or eviction is likewise not supported, since its pod and deployment are Ready with 0 restarts, so the 503s are not restart artifacts.

Rejected: the NetworkChaos experiments otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition-* caused this alert. They started at 10:25:49, about 22 minutes after the first 503 UC against the frontend upstream at 10:03:07 and after further 503s at 10:17:43 and 10:21:11/10:21:59, and they target two fraud-detection pods and the kafka pod, not the frontend pod or the frontend-proxy path; they can explain fraud-detection's own small error signal but not the frontend-proxy 503s.

Leading mechanism (hypothesis, unverified): the frontend Next.js container accepts the connection but terminates it before producing a response, so no frontend span is created and Envoy records UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; the internal reason is unconfirmed because the frontend container produced no log lines in any queried window, leaving app-level panics or aborted handlers unknown.

Second candidate (hypothesis, correlation only): the frontend container's 100m CPU limit leaves it CFS-throttled in 31-35% of periods at 4.3-6.8 throttled periods per second, stalling the Node.js event loop and dropping in-flight request sockets. Counter-indications: throttling is flat across the measured window, no throttling burst coincides with the 503 clusters, and no pre-10:04 baseline exists for this pod.

Third candidate (hypothesis, no supporting evidence found): a node-level kube-proxy or conntrack problem on node i-029c97e90b3730286, where both frontend-proxy and frontend run, terminates individual connections. No NetworkPolicy object was returned for otel-demo, no chaos experiment targets the frontend pod, the nodes are Ready and pressure-free, and the frontend Service has a single ready endpoint, so this remains unevidenced.

Fourth candidate (hypothesis, largely excluded by the evidence at hand): a fault-injection flag was switched on. The flagd-config ConfigMap shows all twelve fault flags at defaultVariant "off", none of them declares connection termination on the frontend path, so only a runtime flagd change not reflected in the ConfigMap could qualify, and runtime flagd state could not be read.

Human follow-up (advice): raise or split the frontend container CPU limit (currently 100m) and enable container-level application logging, then observe whether the 503 UC rate on the frontend upstream falls.

Human follow-up (advice): inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy configuration for the 'frontend' cluster (route timeout, retries, upstream keep-alive and max requests per connection) together with the frontend HTTP server keep-alive and headers timeouts, since that is the connection being terminated before a response starts.

Human follow-up (advice): read flagd's live flag state through its API or UI rather than the ConfigMap alone, and review the RequestErrorRate rule definition, because the annotated 1.1% error ratio could not be reproduced from the available series and the observed frontend-proxy ingress error fraction is roughly 0.03-0.1%.

gaps: The frontend container produced no log lines in the windows queried (fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data for 09:49-09:55, 10:26-10:35 and with a filter for 10:15-10:45), so application-level errors, panics or aborted handlers inside frontend could not be read and the reason the frontend side terminates connections is unverified.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not found (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned status no_data), so the alert expression, window and threshold are unknown and the annotated value 0.01111111111111111 (1.1%) cannot be reconciled with the observed frontend-proxy ingress error fraction.

The log query for '503 UC|upstream_reset' over 09:49-10:03 returned no matching lines but that view had status no_data and its read was cut by the 4 MiB limit, so whether 503s occurred before 10:03:07 is not established; the earliest observed instance is 10:03:07.225.

Kubernetes events were only available with timestamps 10:10:13-10:37:59, so chaos or scheduling activity before 10:10 is unknown and an earlier round of the same NetworkChaos schedule on the frontend path can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
The frontend-proxy access-log stream as read ended at 10:38:47 while spans continue to 10:44:50, so access-log lines after that point are unknown.
No NetworkPolicy objects were returned for otel-demo (kubernetes_jq_query kind=networkpolicies returned status no_data), so network-policy-based filtering cannot be confirmed or excluded.
flagd container logs returned no lines (status no_data), so runtime flag evaluation and any flag change outside the ConfigMap could not be verified.

Container-level metrics for frontend and frontend-proxy begin only around 10:03:50-10:05:00, so there is no pre-onset baseline for CPU throttling, memory or error rate, and the ~09:48 rollout of all otel-demo pods cannot be compared with an earlier revision because change_history is not integrated and no earlier pod exists to inspect.

Node-level conntrack or TCP-reset counters are not among the available metrics (the metric-name query for http_, envoy_, nginx_ and app_ prefixes returned status no_data), so a network-path cause on node i-029c97e90b3730286 could be neither confirmed nor excluded.
The request-level denominator behind the alert is unknown: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans per operation, not unique requests, so no exact error percentage is asserted.
The frontend-proxy and frontend pods have no previous container instance (the tool reported previous terminated container not found), so pre-restart behaviour of these containers is unavailable.
next_steps: Have a human raise the frontend CPU limit (currently 100m) or add frontend replicas and observe whether frontend-proxy 503 UC frequency falls.
Enable verbose application logging on the frontend (Next.js) container and read its stderr/stdout for 'http: panic', socket hang-up or unhandled-rejection lines during 10:03-10:45.
Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy configuration for the 'frontend' cluster (timeouts, retries, keep-alive settings) and the frontend HTTP server keep-alive and headers timeouts.
Review the RequestErrorRate alert rule and its ratio calculation to confirm what the 1.1% annotation actually measures.
Check flagd's live flag state through its API or UI for flags changed outside the ConfigMap during the window.
Confirm from platform change history, which is not integrated in this Run, whether anything changed at the ~09:48 rollout or near 10:03 affecting the frontend pod's networking or resources.
